title: EvidenceRecord
description:
The evidence-integrity spec's own record kind: the candidate shape
[`crate::evidence::validate_evidence`] validates. Carries whichever
join keys are relevant to what it attests (join-spine `task_id`
row: task ↔ evidence ↔ trajectory). `project_id` is OPTIONAL
(design D6: real records may exist via `canon gate promote` before
every producer is project-aware). The native trust/evidence fields are
the home for what were `canon-gate`-owned raw-JSON companions (design
D9), and `approval` is the explicit accountable attestation for this
phase. Each companion reads THREE-way: a legitimately ABSENT key
deserializes to `None`/empty (the documented safe default —
`canon-gate` still owns what that default MEANS per field, e.g.
absent `lifecycle` = draft), a PRESENT well-formed value deserializes
typed, and a PRESENT malformed value fails this whole record's
`Deserialize` — never silently collapsed to absent.

audit.description:
Present only on an audit record (`--kind audit`, 0.15 D3): the
external evaluator and its result. Additive.

brief_override.description:
Present only on a record attested under `--override-reason` while
a subject it attests for had an enforced, unapproved brief (0.16
M7). Additive.

code_tree.description:
The git tree id of the code the writing command saw (0.28 D7b):
the working tree for the default `HEAD`, the commit's own code for
an explicit rev; `.canon/`, spec roots and `code.exclude` are not
part of it. Absent on a record written before 0.28.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

worktree_dirty.description:
Whether the working tree's code differed from `HEAD`'s when this was
written (0.28 D7b). Absent on a record written before 0.28.

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

AuditResult.description:
What an external evaluator concluded when it re-audited a scenario's
declared success (0.15 D3). `Indeterminate` is a real outcome — the
evaluator ran and could not decide — never an approval.

oneOf.description: The evaluator re-checked the requirement and the declared success holds.
The evaluator found the declared success false (a counterexample).
The evaluator ran but could not decide either way.

BriefOverride.description:
The accountable waiver an attestation was let through under, when
`canon evidence add` refused it because a subject it attests for has
an enforced, unapproved brief (0.16 M7) and the operator passed
`--override-reason`. [`StatusOverride`]'s shape without `to`: an
attestation moves no status. `waived` lists the refusals it let
through as `(unreviewed-promotion, <subject id>)`, the pair the ship
guard's brief check prints.

waived.description: Exactly the brief refusals this waiver let through, sorted.

EvidenceApproval.description:
An approval attestation attached to an [`EvidenceRecord`].

`verified` is retained only as a non-authoritative display field for wire
compatibility. Gate decisions MUST reverify `signature` over the canonical
artifact-bound payload and MUST ignore this bit and process environment.

signature.description: Detached SSH signature in armored form. Missing signatures never count.

subject.description: Subject and artifact binding covered by the signature.

EvidenceAttachment.description:
A file an [`EvidenceRecord`] is bound to (experimental evidence
binding). Canon reads the file when the evidence is added — it never
executes anything — and records what it found: the bytes' sha256, and
for a parsed report the case it matched and that case's outcome. The
digest lets a reviewer later confirm exactly which file backed the
claim; an attachment with no `format` is an opaque artifact (a trace,
screenshots, an agent QA log) bound by digest alone.

case.description: The report case this evidence was matched to (parsed reports only).

path.description: Repository-relative path, `/`-separated, as read at attestation.

sha256.description: 64 lowercase hex characters: sha256 over the file's bytes.

EvidenceAudit.description:
An external evaluator's re-audit of a scenario (0.15 D3), carried on
an [`EvidenceRecord`] written by `canon evidence audit`.
Canon never generates or runs the audit; it records which evaluator
ran (id, version, and the sha256 of the evaluator itself) and what it
concluded. A record carrying this is an AUDITED outcome and is folded
apart from declared evidence: it never becomes a scenario's latest
declared verdict.

evaluator_digest.description:
64 lowercase hex characters: sha256 of the evaluator (its binary,
image, or prompt bundle), as the evaluator's operator reports it.

EvidenceVerdict.description:
The three-way verdict an evidence record carries. `Divergent` is an
explicit third value rather than "no record exists" — the donor
parity harness represents non-faithful as *absence* of a
design-review/code-review record, which works for a directory-scanned
ledger but not for a single, standalone canon record whose own
`Deserialize` must always succeed or fail on its own — so canon makes
the state explicit instead of leaning on record-absence.

FlaggedOverlay.description:
The orthogonal `flagged` overlay, paired with whatever
`EvidenceRecord` it marks. `flagged_by`/`flagged_at` carry who/when;
the flag-CLEAR ratchet's enforcement (only a human-attributed actor
may set or clear this, one-way) lives in `canon-gate::trust`
(`attempt_clear`), not here — this type carries the shape only.

ProjectId.description: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` — lowercase alnum + hyphen, first character alphanumeric, no underscore (keeps the `__` natural-key separator unambiguous) — joins: not a join-spine key; composite identity prefix on Scenario/Review/Divergence natural keys (`<project_id>__<scenario_id>…`), optional on EvidenceRecord

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

ReportFormat.description:
The machine-readable test-report formats `canon evidence add
--report` parses (experimental evidence binding). Canon never runs a
test; it reads the report the team's own runner already wrote.

oneOf.description: JUnit XML — emitted or convertible from nearly every ecosystem.
Cucumber JSON — Gherkin runners; scenario tags travel in it.

Swift Testing's JSON-lines event stream (`swift test
--experimental-event-stream-output <path>`): the scenario id is
read from a test's display name, else its function name.

ReportOutcome.description: The outcome a parsed report records for the case an attachment names.

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

RunId.description: ULID (Crockford base32, 26 chars) — joins: run ↔ events ↔ manifest

ScenarioId.description: `<area>.<surface>.<nn>` — `[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.\d{2,}`; never renumbered once assigned — joins: spec ↔ test ↔ ledger ↔ divergence

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

Sha.description: git commit SHA-1: exactly 40 lowercase hex characters — joins: reward signals ↔ trajectory

TaskId.description: `<change_id>#<n>`, where `<n>` is one or more dot-separated integers (`1`, `1.1`, `6.2`) matching `tasks.md`'s own numbering — joins: task ↔ evidence ↔ trajectory

TotalOrder.description: monotonic fold-ordering rank (e.g. Divergence.run_seq) — the SOLE primary sort key within a fold group; never compared against a round tiebreak

TrustLifecycle.description:
The three-rung evidence lifecycle — exactly one per artifact, never
a fourth "flagged" rung ([`FlaggedOverlay`] is an orthogonal
overlay, not a lifecycle state). Unlike the donor's freeform
`@draft`/`@reviewed`/`@ratified` tags (which can co-occur), a typed
Rust enum makes "two lifecycle tags at once" structurally
impossible.

WaivedViolation.description:
One violation a [`StatusOverride`] let through: the gate failure
class (`unreviewed-promotion`, `open-blocker`) and the violation's
subject (a scenario id, or `<change_id>#<round>.<seq>` for a
blocker), as `canon gate check` prints them.
